To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parents' accounts suggest health visiting services outside the home can be valuable in supporting parents and their children's health and well-being.
health visiting services in which health visitors are able to work outside the home are valued by families, and that this work is particularly important for families with complex needs.

parents' accounts of support from health visitors and children's centres staff were characterized by the importance of relationships and of the staff being ‘there’ for parents and children, and that these features were associated with parents feeling empowered in relation to their own parenting, and with children's development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature and value of the support that health visitors can offer families in the home and in community settings.
the ways that health visiting can be understood and practised as a relational activity.
understanding how parents' experiences of family support outside of their homes can help them to develop a sense of autonomy in relation to their children and to their parenting role.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

health visitors and children's centres can play an important role in supporting parents and families in their everyday lives, particularly in the early years of their children's lives, and that this support is likely to be most effective where it is responsive to parents' needs and preferences and where health visitors and children centres are embedded in local communities.
the support offered outside the home was perceived to be beneficial to parents, and to their children's health and development.
parents' experiences of family support outside their homes were generally very positive, but that there were some important caveats to be borne in mind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parents' experiences with health visiting outside the homes were positive and that the support they received was valued.

health visiting services are valued by parents for the support they provide, and that this support is most valued when it is delivered by health visitors who have a good understanding of parents' circumstances and needs.
health visiting is a valuable and effective service that is under threat.
The main takeaway from our work is that

health visiting and family support services are not only valuable in terms of their contribution to child and family health and development, they also contribute to parents' sense of themselves as autonomous individuals.

the health visiting service is a key element in the provision of support to families with young children in the UK, and that this support is best understood in terms of the relational autonomy of families.
health visiting services should not only focus on supporting parents in their role in caring for their child, but also on helping them to become more confident and autonomous in their own lives.
